 ORDER
Counsel for the petitioners contends that in terms of the policy dated 12.11.2014 the land of petitioners, was sought to be acquired through their mutual consent.
Accordingly the proceedings were initiated in terms of the policy and upon inspection, carried out by the Patwari which has been brought on record at page no.32 the land was found to be irrigated.
Accordingly, the beneficiary department also prepared a cheque of compensation and forwarded the same to the Collector vide communication dated 17.07.2017 contained in Annexure P/12.

Unfortunately, the Collector, vide impugned order dated 09.04.2018 contained in Annexure P/1 while referring to the inspection report dated 18.08.2017 of Sub Divisional Officer cum Land Acquisition Officer concluded that the land was un-irrigated and accordingly had issued direction for computation of compensation while treating the land to be un-irrigated.

It is contended by the counsel for the petitioners that he was not extended any opportunity of hearing when the inspection dated 18.05.2017 was carried out by Sub Divisional Officer cum Land Acquisition Officer Panna nor he was aware about any inspection dated 18.08.2017.

It is contended by the counsel that there was no occasion to submit a report afresh when there was already a report which is brought on record at page no.32 and the same was acted upon the beneficiary department and a cheque of Rs.10,31,360/- was forwarded to the Collector Panna towards the compensation while treating the land to be irrigated.
It is thus submitted that impugned order contained in Annexure P/1 deserves to be quashed and the respondent be, directed to pay the compensation as forwarded by the beneficiary department i.e.
Public
Works Department vide Annexure P/12 dated 17.07.2017.

Per contra, counsel for the respondents submit that the order of Collector is based on the inspection report submitted by the Sub Divisional Officer dated 18.08.2017 and in the said report it was concluded by Sub Divisional Officer that the land was un-irrigated and accordingly the Collector has passed the order on the basis of report dated 18.08.2017 and, therefore, submit that no interference is warranted.
Heard rival submissions and perused the record.
In the present case, the petitioners have brought on record a report of the patwari which is at page no.32 and the same has not been disputed by the respondents in their return.
In the report of the patwari, it was concluded that land is irrigated.

It further appears that the said report was acted upon and was duly accepted by the beneficiary department and a cheque was also prepared and forwarded to Collector Panna vide communication dated 17.07.2017 contained in Annexure P/12.

sentences.text: The petitioners do not dispute that this amount of compensation which is mentioned in Annexure P/12 was computed while treating the land to be irrigated, therefore, so far as the amount mentioned in communication dated 17.07.2017 is concerned, the petitioners have no grievance.
Undisputedly, the respondents have failed to demonstrate as to whether the petitioners were extended any opportunity while carrying out inspection on 18.05.2017 by Sub Divisional Officer.
No inspection could have been carried out behind the back of the petitioners in asmuch, as the rights of the petitioners have direct nexus with compensation in terms of the policy dated 12.11.2014.

The entire order of the Collector does not deal with the report of the patwari which has been brought on record at page 32 of the petition and, therefore, the Collector was required to take into consideration the said report and also the fact that the said report was accepted by the beneficiary department and the cheque was also forwarded to the Collector District Panna way back on 17.07.2017.

In view of the aforesaid, the order impugned dated 09.04.2018 contained in P/1 is quashed and the matter is remitted back to the Collector Distt. Panna to take a decision afresh while taking into consideration the report which has been brought on record at page no.32, and to decide the controversy afresh while extending the opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and all concerned.

It is needless to emphasise that the Collector shall also take into consideration the factum that the said report was accepted by the beneficiary department and the cheque was already issued on 17.07.2017.
The entire exercise shall be carried out within a period of 90 days from today.
With the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed off.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE VPA Bhulai Gond vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100189856/
